chunks: Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, from Khattab ibn Salama, who said:

I went to him — meaning Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) — and I intended to complain to him about what I was enduring from my wife because of her bad character. But he spoke to me first and said:

'My father had once given me in marriage to a woman of bad character. So I complained of that to him, and he said to me: What prevents you from separating from her? God has placed that matter in your hands.' So I said to myself: 'He has relieved me.'

key_terms.سُوءِ خُلُقِهَا: Evil/bad character — the legal and moral ground for seeking divorce in this chapter
key_terms.فَرَّجَ: To relieve/remove distress — used here to express the narrator's inner sense of liberation
key_terms.فِرَاق: Separation/divorce — the permissible remedy prescribed by God

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Kadhim say about divorcing a wife with bad character?
ai.summary: Khattab ibn Salama visited Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) intending to complain about his wife's poor character. In a remarkable display of foreknowledge, the Imam preempted him by sharing a parallel personal experience: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) had once advised the Imam himself to divorce a wife of bad character, affirming that God has granted men the right of divorce. This narrative highlights the Imam's miraculous awareness, validates divorce as a permissible remedy for marital incompatibility, and reflects the teaching context of the chapter on divorcing an incompatible spouse.

married me to/gave me in marriage to

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Mahran, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Umar Bin Abdul Aziz, from Khattab Bin Salma who said,

‘I went over to him<sup>asws</sup>, meaning Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, and I wanted to complain to him<sup>asws</sup> what I faced from my wife from the evil of her mannerisms. So he<sup>asws</sup> began before me, so he<sup>asws</sup> said:

‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> had got me<sup>asws</sup> married once to a woman of evil manners. So I<sup>asws</sup> complained of that to him<sup>asws</sup>, so he<sup>asws</sup> said to me<sup>asws</sup>: ‘What is preventing you from separating from her. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Made that (Permissible) to you<sup>asws</sup>?’ So I said in what is between me and myself, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> has relieved me’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ahmad ibn Mehran has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali from ‘Umar ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz from Khattab ibn Salmah who has said the following: “
I once went to see him, abu al-Hassan, Musa, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and complain before him against my wife because of her bad moral behaviors. He (the Imam) initiating to speak to me said, ‘

One time my father arranged for me the marriage to a woman who had very bad moral behaviors and I complained before him against her. He said, ‘What stops you from divorcing her? Allah has already given you such authority.’ I (the narrator) then said to myself, ‘You (Imam) by Allah have provided relief and a way out for me.’”
